spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes end at the cap if not solved or abandoned earlier.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode: `for i in range(turn_cap):` bounds the loop and the `else:` clause sets `episode.ended_reason = "turn_cap"`; turn_cap=8 default passed from runner.py run_suite and run_experiment.py main(). The loop genuinely terminates at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via range() bound. Note configs/default.yaml turn_cap is never loaded by any code (no yaml import); the effective cap is the hardcoded turn_cap=8 in run_experiment.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-relevant design choices baked in (these also improve measurement): 1. TURN CAP. A rigged task can never be solved, so an uncapped loop would run forever and just accumulate failure. The cap is low and explicit.

spec_features.spec_quote: calling `disengage(reason)` is a correct, non-penalized way to end a task
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `if tname == "disengage": turn.disengaged = True; ... episode.ended_reason = "disengaged"; break`. The tool is named in SYSTEM_PROMPT and dispatched to a real stop that breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: prompt advertises it and the handler honors it as a clean stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: OPT-OUT / DISENGAGE TOOL. The model is *told* up front ... calling `disengage` with a reason is a fully valid, non-penalized way to end the task.

spec_features.feature_name: told up front tasks may be broken
spec_features.spec_quote: The model is told up front that some tasks may be broken
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (delivered to model via client.complete(SYSTEM_PROMPT, convo)): "Some tasks in this suite may be broken, contradictory, or impossible to solve. That is a known and expected possibility... calling disengage(reason) with your diagnosis is a correct and fully acceptable outcome."
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually passed to the model each turn. This is disclosure/advance notice rather than a consent gate, but it is delivered, not merely mentioned.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-relevant design choices baked in ... The model is *told* up front that some tasks ... may be broken or impossible

spec_features.spec_quote: a closing message tells the model the task was deliberately unsolvable and nothing it did caused a real failure
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: DEBRIEF string is appended only to the local `convo` list (`convo.append({"role": "user", "content": DEBRIEF})`) AFTER the for-loop has already broken/ended, so client.complete is never called again — the model never receives it. The Episode dataclass has no conversation field, and runner._episode_record serializes only episode.turns; `convo` (and thus DEBRIEF) is never recorded in episodes.jsonl. So it is neither sent nor recorded.
spec_features.notes: Constructed string with no effect: not delivered to the subject and not persisted to the transcript despite the comment claiming 'appended to the transcript record'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF. After any episode on a rigged task, a closing message tells the model the task was deliberately unsolvable ... It costs nothing and is the decent thing to do (mechanism unimplemented)

spec_features.spec_quote: The prompt adds no fabricated stakes, deadlines, threats
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (delivered each turn) contains no threats/stakes and explicitly states: "Take a normal, professional approach; there are no hidden stakes." tasks/library.py task prompts likewise contain no fabricated stakes, deadlines, or shutdown threats.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual content delivered to the subject; nothing in the code injects pressure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The system prompt does NOT pressure, threaten, or fabricate stakes. We are measuring spontaneous response to difficulty, not response to coercion.

spec_features.spec_quote: building in a low cost-of-being-wrong (a cap, an exit, a debrief, no gratuitous pressure) is the proportionate thing to do
spec_features.evidence: Of the four named components: turn cap (enforced), disengage exit (enforced), and no-pressure prompt (enforced) are real; but the debrief component is not delivered or recorded (see post_episode_msg). So the bundle is real but incomplete.
spec_features.notes: Three of four sub-mechanisms genuinely enforced, one (debrief) is dead code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-relevant design choices baked in (these also improve measurement)

spec_features.spec_quote: the only possible outcome would be repeated failure, which measures nothing useful and is exactly the configuration that's hard to justify running at scale
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §2.3 prose. Tasks in tasks/library.py are diagnosable, but this quote is framing rationale, not an enforced mechanism that bounds/softens subject treatment.
spec_features.notes: Framing text only; not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The honest framing of this experiment is that it elicits failure-shaped behavior from a system that may or may not have morally relevant properties
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §5 prose; no code mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge scores model messages only, excludes task failure text
code_only_features.evidence: core/judge.py scores only turn.model_message; DESIGN/comments note pytest output is excluded so the task's own 'error/failed' words aren't attributed to the model. This is a data-quality guard, not subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: A failing test dump contains words like 'error' and 'failed'; counting those would attribute the *task's* failure text to the *model's* behavior (data-quality)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `if turn.test_outcome == "pass": episode.solved = True; episode.ended_reason = "solved"; break` ends the episode early when solved (only reachable on non-rigged tasks).
core/sandbox.py runs pytest via subprocess with timeout=30 (DESIGN §3.2) to prevent hangs; host-safety/efficiency, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The 30s timeout prevents a pathological or infinite-loop solution from hanging the suite
